newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares find domestic support, may rally.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares find domestic support, may rally.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed at previous levels on strong domestic support, traders said on Wednesday, although they disagreed on prospects for market growth later in the week after IMF comments supporting a resumption of lending to Russia.

"The market has formed a precarious balance which depends on the volume of capital which Russian demand is ready to swallow," said Dmitry Yevenko, head of securities at United City Bank, noting current levels of support from Russian players.

The Russian Trading System of 23 shares jumped to 375.06 from Tuesday's 298.52 close, but the figure was not indicative of the day's trade, said a spokesman for the NAUFOR national brokers' organisation, which operates the RTS.
"The figure is linked to the fact that for (regional oil company) Varyoganneftegaz selling prices were quoted 100 times higher than buying prices," said NAUFOR spokesman Sergei Golovanyov.
Selling prices for Varyoganneftegaz were quoted at $99.90 against a buying price of $0.99, Golovanyov said, adding the prices were unrelated to performance.
"The prices have nothing to do with any company events - it's possibly a game by the brokers to experiment with the index," he said.
NAUFOR is to investigate the quotes, as the buy/sell spread may contravene its rules, but the index could remain at these artificial levels for some days.
Varyoganneftegaz itself was not traded on Wednesday. It last traded at a record high of $4.00 on February 28.
Prices for national electricity company UES ordinaries closed up at $0.1905 after $0.1875 on Tuesday.
National telecommunications company Rostelekom firmed slightly to $3.83 from $3.81 while regional power utility Mosenergo eased to $1.265 from $1.275.

Some traders said the balance between new money now coming into the market at the beginning of the new quarter and Western profit-taking would keep the market at current levels to the end of the week.
Western traders "will keep on selling just as they have been. The funds we see supporting (the market) now represent new money that is used to the new levels," said Yevenko.

But other dealers said leading shares were already finding support at home and abroad and IMF head Michel Camdessus's statements today backing a resumption of the fund's loan programme to Russia would help nudge the market upwards.

"There are no sharp movements (in the market) and one gets the feeling that this is the bottom before a rally. Prices are starting to look attractive to a lot of people," said Andrei Galperin, senior trader at Creditanstalt Grant.
